card.name: Lead-in to NSAID risk-factor lists
card.fires_on: Words like "with", "include" or a semicolon that come right before a list of risk factors or at-risk conditions in NSAID warnings. It marks the spot where the next risk factor is about to be named.

modes.label: "with" before conditions
modes.description: The word "with" introduces patients with a named condition, such as impaired renal function, at greater risk of a reaction.
modes.example: Patients at greater risk of this reaction are those<< with>> impaired renal function, heart failure, liver

modes.label: Semicolon between risk factors
modes.description: A semicolon or closing bracket and semicolon separates items in a run of risk factors for GI bleeding.
modes.example: Other factors that increase the risk of GI bleeding in patients treated with NSAIDs include longer duration of NSAID therapy<<;>> concomitant use of oral cortic

card.plain: It lights up just before the next risk factor in a list of things that raise a patient's risk on NSAIDs.
